text:
alex: Hey team — hitting a 400 when invoking a tool via function-calling. Error in response: "Invalid JSON in \u2018tool_args\u2019: unexpected token at position 45". Using our JS SDK via node.

maria-support: Can you paste the payload you sent? SDK call + raw body would help.

alex: Pasting the snippet I send (trimmed):
```
const payload = {
  model: 'redwood-1',
  input: 'read file',
  functions: [ { name: 'read_file', args_schema: { path: 'string' } } ],
  tool_call: { name: 'read_file', args: "{\"path\":\"C:\\Users\\alex\\notes.txt\", \"encoding\":\"utf-8\", }" }
};
```

Note: I was passing args as a JSON string because the example I copied used a raw JSON-string in the `tool_call.args` field. The file path has backslashes. I also suspect my editor added a BOM earlier on.

sam-eng: Ok two issues here: (1) You're passing `args` as a string (double-encoded). The runtime expects an actual JSON object for `tool_call.args` (not a string). (2) There's a trailing comma after `"utf-8"` which makes the JSON invalid. Also backslashes in Windows paths must be escaped (you did `\\` in the string, which double-escapes because it's a string literal).

maria-support: Minimal repro if you want to test quickly: send this curl (note args is a JSON object, not a string):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/call -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1","tool_call":{"name":"read_file","args":{"path":"C:/Users/alex/notes.txt","encoding":"utf-8"}}}'
```

Also ensure your editor isn't inserting a BOM (\uFEFF) at the start of the payload. That can make the parser choke before the first brace.

alex: Ah, I see. My code was doing `JSON.stringify(args)` into a string field and the SDK then serialized the whole payload again. That explains the double-encoding and the trailing comma slipped in from a manual edit.

julie: For BOM detection you can run: `if (payload[0] === '\\uFEFF') payload = payload.slice(1)`. On node when reading files, `fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` shouldn't include BOM normally, but some editors do.

ops-oncall-bot: Documentation: https://docs.redwood.ai/docs/function-calling#tool-arguments-schema (see "args must be an object" and examples).

sam-eng: TL;DR fixes: (1) pass args as an object, not as a string, (2) remove trailing commas, (3) normalize Windows paths or use forward slashes, (4) strip BOM if present.

alex: Tested the curl above — success. No 400. Thanks! :tada:

maria-support: Marking as resolved in our side. If you want, we can add an SDK runtime check to throw a clearer error when args is a string (tracking: SDK-458). :thumbsup:

alex: That'd help. Thanks everyone.
